objective: Expose checked finite-field quotient/FGLM operations in Python and support independently verified partial/full polynomial specialization.

implementation.quotient: Public GroebnerBasis.fglm, quotient_basis and multiplication_matrix use the existing checked GF(p) kernels. Complete quotient directions, nilpotents, original ideal, typed generators and coefficient/output policies remain bound.
implementation.evaluation: Sparse contraction uses binary modular powers; a separate verifier reconstructs every coefficient by repeated multiplication and signed column sums. Output characteristic and exact remaining typed generator order are checked.
implementation.python: Poly/PurePoly scalar, explicit generator/index, leading sequence and ordered mapping evaluation uses one cumulative native request. Scalar results and checked empty-assignment identity preserve public conventions.
implementation.regressions: Native forged-candidate/ring/assignment and resource-limit tests; public source/control/container mutation and terminal-failure tests; evaluation-to-inferred-field-Groebner/FGLM/operator integration over both nilpotent GF(3) fibers.
implementation.baseline_repair: Replace the stale empty-generator-ring refusal expectation with stronger constant-field admission, residue and forged-certificate tests. Existing constructor contract explicitly permits F_p as a constant field.

validation.dependencies: Exact registered donor revisions and locked Cargo graph; manifests and lockfile unchanged.
validation.python_syntax: Affected Python sources and regression files parsed successfully.
validation.independent_review: Separate implementation, test/build and root review of source binding, verifier independence, bounds, output metadata and mutation checks; the mapping length check was moved before copying a mutated mapping.

oracle.evaluation: Public selector/container, field representative, PurePoly and empty-assignment conventions checked in isolation. Both GF(3) integration bases and all multiplication-operator columns checked by exact reduction.
oracle.scope: Oracle fixtures only; not execution of the FrankenSymPy extension.

validation.remote_verification: Both feature commits fetched independently through GitHub; exact SHAs, messages, changed paths and feature diff checked.

limitations: Ordinary multiplication-matrix entries are integer residue representatives; later matrix operations require reduction modulo p.
Noninteger or approximate evaluation and extension fields remain unsupported.
Prime-field quotient minimal_polynomial, invert and syzygies remain unsupported.
In-process independently checked receipts are not portable proof-kernel certificates.
